title: What If the Sun Never Set? It Already Doesn't in Norway

scenes.text: What if the Sun never set? Parts of the Arctic live it. The twist is sleep.
Earth's axis tilts about 23.4 degrees, so in summer the Arctic leans toward the Sun all day.
Tromso, Norway, gets more than two months of midnight sun. The North Pole gets about 186 days.
Visitors often sleep badly for two to four nights, and most adapt within about a week.
A study of 21,083 residents found no seasonal change in sleep duration.
Researchers think city lights may blunt the swing. Even endless daylight barely changes how long we sleep.

description:
What if the Sun never set?
Above the Arctic Circle it doesn't for weeks, yet a big Tromso study found sleep duration barely moved.
